title: No Kings rallies held in Washington and nationwide ahead of midterms

tea.why: Protesters gathered to voice opposition to President Donald Trump's presidency during nationwide demonstrations.
tea.want: Participants aimed to encourage early voting among citizens ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.
tea.changed: Oct 18: Meta temporarily disabled the No Kings Coalition Instagram account during nationwide demonstrations, later restoring it.

summary: Demonstrations organized by the No Kings network took place across the United States, including Washington, D.C., and all 50 states on Saturday. The events were designed to encourage early voting ahead of the November midterm elections while opposing President Donald Trump's presidency. In Washington, participants gathered at the Lincoln Memorial featuring music and signs with slogans such as 'VOTE EARLY' and 'HANDS OFF MY VOTE!'. Similar actions occurred in other cities, such as Atlanta. The coalition, which emerged following the president's return to office, experienced a temporary suspension of its primary Instagram account by Meta during the protests due to an automated safety filter, though the company later apologized and restored the page.
demands: Vote early in the midterm elections
response: Meta stated that the temporary suspension of the No Kings Coalition Instagram account was an error caused by an automated safety filter triggered by high posting frequencies.

updates.text: No Kings rallies were held in Washington and across major US cities to encourage early voting.
Meta temporarily disabled the No Kings Coalition Instagram account during the nationwide actions, citing an automated safety filter error.
